================================
USING YOUR OWN POSTGRESQL SERVER
================================

  Only read this if you set ERP_DB_MODE=host. If the database runs in Docker
  (ERP_DB_MODE=docker), everything here is done for you and you can ignore
  this file.

  Do all of this before running the installer. It checks each of these points
  and stops with a clear message rather than starting a half-configured
  system.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

What is required
================

  Version
  Requirement: PostgreSQL 15. Versions 14 and 16 are not tested and are not
      supported.

  Database
  Requirement: A database used by nothing else, and empty at first install

  Login role
  Requirement: A role that owns that database

  Privileges
  Requirement: Ordinary ownership. No superuser rights are needed, and no
      extensions are installed

  Reachability
  Requirement: The server must accept connections from Docker on this machine

  > Why a database of its own. The application manages its own tables and
    refuses to adopt a database it does not recognise. Pointing it at a
    database that already holds other data will fail partway through. It costs
    nothing to create a separate database.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Create the database and its login
====================================

  Connect as a PostgreSQL administrator (usually the postgres user) and run:

      CREATE ROLE erp WITH LOGIN PASSWORD 'put-a-long-random-password-here';
      CREATE DATABASE erp OWNER erp;

  Use a long random password. On Linux or macOS:

      openssl rand -base64 32

  That password goes into .env as ERP_DB_PASSWORD - the installer asks you for
  it.

  If your organisation requires different names, use them, and put your names
  into .env as ERP_DB_NAME and ERP_DB_USER.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2. Let the server accept connections
====================================

  Docker containers reach your database from a private internal network, so
  PostgreSQL must be told to accept them. Two files control this.

  Find where they are:

      SHOW config_file;    -- postgresql.conf
      SHOW hba_file;       -- pg_hba.conf

  In postgresql.conf - make sure the server listens beyond its own loopback:

      listen_addresses = '*'

  In pg_hba.conf - add a rule permitting the Docker network. Put it before any
  broader reject rule:

      # TYPE  DATABASE  USER  ADDRESS         METHOD
      host    erp       erp   172.16.0.0/12   scram-sha-256

  172.16.0.0/12 is the address range Docker uses for its internal networks. If
  your database is on a different machine from OrbixERP, use that machine's
  address instead, for example 192.168.1.50/32.

  Apply the changes:

      sudo systemctl reload postgresql      # Linux
  On Windows, restart the postgresql-x64-15 service from the Services panel.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3. Open the firewall
====================

  If the database is on another machine, allow TCP port 5432 from OrbixERP
  machine.

  - Linux: sudo ufw allow from <erp-machine-ip> to any port 5432
  - Windows: Windows Defender Firewall -> Inbound Rules -> New Rule -> Port ->
    TCP 5432

  If the database is on the same machine as OrbixERP, no firewall change is
  normally needed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4. Answer the installer
=======================

  Question: Database server address
  Answer: host.docker.internal if PostgreSQL is on this same machine;
      otherwise its hostname or IP

  Question: Port
  Answer: 5432

  Question: Database name
  Answer: erp (or your name)

  Question: Login role
  Answer: erp (or your role)

  Question: Password
  Answer: the one you set in step 1

  > What host.docker.internal means. It is a special name meaning "the
    computer this software is running on". It is needed because the
    application runs inside a container, where localhost refers to the
    container itself and not to your machine. The configuration already
    contains the setting that makes this name work on Linux as well as on
    Windows and macOS.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Encrypted connections
=====================

  If your database requires TLS, add this to .env:

      ERP_DB_URL_PARAMS=?sslmode=require

  For a private certificate authority, use
  ?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=/path/to/ca.crt and make the certificate
  available inside the container - ask your supplier for help with that step.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Your responsibilities in this mode
==================================

  Choosing your own database means these become yours:

  - Backups. orbixerp backup still works and writes into backups/, but you may
    prefer your own tooling. Either way, verify a restore actually works - an
    untested backup is a guess.
  - Availability. If the database is down, OrbixERP will not start.
  - Upgrades. Stay on PostgreSQL 15. Do not upgrade the major version without
    checking with your supplier first.
  - Capacity. Monitor disk space. A full disk stops OrbixERP writing anything
    at all.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Checking it yourself
====================

  To test the connection the same way the installer does, without installing
  any tools:

      docker run --rm --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
        -e PGPASSWORD='your-password' postgres:15-alpine \
        psql -h host.docker.internal -p 5432 -U erp -d erp -c '\conninfo'

  If that prints connection details, OrbixERP will connect too. If it does
  not, the error tells you which of the steps above still needs attention.
